We have full resolution with t_last under 10 min, so the only possible improvement is to make the method faster without losing any pair below R = 1.5. Shortening tG by one step is the most direct test of the speed limit while keeping the successful phi window and temperature unchanged.

Since tG = 8 lost resolution at the 3/4 pair, keep the successful 10 min slope but narrow the gradient window slightly from the high-organic end to reduce steepness and potentially gain a margin on the limiting pair while staying under 10 min. The 0.20–0.45, 8 min method is fully resolved with some time headroom, so lowering phi1 one more step tests whether the window can be tightened further without incurring the >10 min penalty. This is the most informative remaining local refinement around the new short, full-score method.

With two injections left and several 1.000 methods already found, the best use is to test one last nearby window that might keep full resolution while offering additional robustness on the critical 3/4 pair. Lowering phi0 to 0.15 from the successful 0.20–0.45, 8 min condition is the most informative remaining local adjustment.

For the final shot, test whether the proven 0.25–0.45, 25 C window can be shortened one more step from 8 to 6 min while retaining full resolution, since this is the only remaining way to improve practical speed beyond the existing 1.000 methods. If it fails, the campaign still ends with several perfect methods already in hand.
